Small Node service, five files under `src/`, no framework — just `node:http`.

```mermaid
graph LR
  server.js -->|verifyToken| auth.js
  server.js -->|route| routes.js
  routes.js -->|cached reads| cache.js
  routes.js -->|writes| store.js
  cache.js -->|loader| store.js
```

- **`server.js`** — raw HTTP server. Every request must carry a `Bearer <userId>.<sig>` header or it gets a 401.
- **`auth.js`** — checks that header with an HMAC signature against a shared secret (`AUTH_SECRET` env var, defaults to `'dev-secret'`).
- **`routes.js`** — a small table mapping `METHOD /path` to a handler: `GET /users`, `GET /orders`, `POST /orders`.
- **`cache.js`** — a 256-entry LRU sitting in front of reads, no expiry of its own.
- **`store.js`** — the "database": an in-memory `Map` where every record expires 15 minutes after it's written.

One thing worth knowing before you touch orders: the comment in `routes.js` says writes invalidate the cache, but `putOrder` never actually clears the `orders:<userId>` cache key. After someone posts an order, `GET /orders` can keep serving the stale list until it ages out of the LRU on its own.
